acquisition.en: the process of learning or getting something
acquisition.ex: Language acquisition is easier for young children.

added.ex: He added that the shop would open late.

advertising.en: showing ads to sell products or services
advertising.ex: The website earns money from advertising.

adverts.en: notices that try to sell something
adverts.ex: There are too many adverts on this app.

advocated.en: publicly supported an idea or plan
advocated.ex: She advocated longer breaks for workers.

example.en: Many doctors advocate a diet rich in vegetables.
example.zh: 許多醫生提倡多吃蔬菜的飲食。

note.meaning: 公開主張；提倡（某政策或做法）。
note.usage: advocate 為及物動詞，直接接名詞或 V-ing，不需加 for（名詞 advocate 才用 for）。

noteEn.meaning: to publicly support a plan, idea or policy.
noteEn.usage: As a verb it takes a direct object: 'advocate reform' (no 'for').

noteEs.exampleTr: Muchos médicos recomiendan una dieta rica en verduras.
noteEs.meaning: defender o promover públicamente una idea.
noteEs.usage: El verbo advocate va seguido directamente de un sustantivo o V-ing.

noteHi.exampleTr: कई डॉक्टर सब्ज़ियों से भरपूर आहार की वकालत करते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: किसी नीति या विचार का सार्वजनिक समर्थन करना।
noteHi.usage: क्रिया advocate के बाद सीधे संज्ञा या V-ing आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 多くの医師は野菜を多く取る食事を推奨している。
noteJa.meaning: 政策や考えを公に支持・提唱する。
noteJa.usage: 動詞 advocate は名詞や動名詞を直接目的語にとる。

noteKo.exampleTr: 많은 의사들이 채소가 풍부한 식단을 권장한다.
noteKo.usage: 동사 advocate는 바로 명사나 동명사를 목적어로 쓴다.

afraid.ex: The little boy was afraid of the dog.

after.en: look after: take care of; be in charge of
after.ja: look after：管理する；面倒を見る

ai.en: computer systems that can think and learn
ai.ex: AI can now write simple emails for you.

also.ex: She speaks French and also some German.

amassing.en: collecting a large amount over time
amassing.ex: He spent years amassing a huge collection of stamps.
amassing.ja: 蓄積すること；集めること

example.en: She amassed a fortune by selling apps.
example.zh: 她靠賣應用程式累積了大筆財富。

note.meaning: （長時間）大量積累；聚斂（金錢、資料等）。
note.usage: 受詞多為 fortune、wealth、evidence、data 等，強調數量龐大。

noteEn.meaning: to collect a large amount of something over time.
noteEn.usage: Often 'amass a fortune', 'amass wealth' or 'amass evidence'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Ella amasó una fortuna vendiendo aplicaciones.
noteEs.meaning: acumular una gran cantidad con el tiempo.
noteEs.usage: Suele usarse con fortune, wealth, evidence.

noteHi.exampleTr: उसने ऐप बेचकर बड़ी दौलत जमा की।
noteHi.meaning: बड़ी मात्रा में धीरे-धीरे इकट्ठा करना।
noteHi.usage: fortune, wealth, evidence जैसे शब्दों के साथ आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 彼女はアプリを売って巨額の財産を築いた。
noteJa.usage: fortune、wealth、evidence などを目的語にとることが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그녀는 앱을 팔아 큰 재산을 모았다.
noteKo.usage: fortune, wealth, evidence 등을 목적어로 자주 쓴다.

amounts.ex: Large amounts of rain fell overnight.

an.en: one; any (article before a vowel sound)

anxiety.en: a feeling of worry and fear

areas.ex: Science and art are very different areas.

argued.en: gave reasons to say something is true
argued.ex: She argued that the plan was too expensive.

around.es: alrededor de; en todo el mundo

as.zh: 作為；as part of：作為…的一部分

asked.en: when someone put a question to her
asked.ex: Asked about the delay, the manager said sorry.

banner.en: under the banner of: as part of
banner.es: bajo el lema de; en el marco de
banner.ex: The groups marched under the banner of peace.
banner.zh: under the banner of：以…名義；在…旗幟下

become.ex: The small café has become very popular.

began.ex: The concert began at eight o'clock.

behind.zh: 在…背後（the company behind：開發…的公司）

better.en: more wisely; in a more useful way
better.ex: You would do better to ask for help.
better.zh: would do better to：最好還是…

big.ex: They live in a big house near the sea.

by.en: used to show who does something or how

call.ex: Parents call for safer roads near schools.

called.ex: Doctors called for a ban on sugary drinks.

came.ex: Many friends came to her birthday party.

cartons.en: paper or plastic boxes for drinks

cautious.ex: Be cautious when you drive in the snow.

central.ex: Family is central to her life.

chances.ex: This job gives young people chances to travel.

change.ex: The weather can change very quickly here.

chatbot.en: a computer program you can chat with
chatbot.ex: The bank's chatbot answered my question quickly.

chatgpt.en: an AI chatbot made by OpenAI

chief.es: jefe; director (chief financial officer: director financiero)
chief.ex: She is the chief engineer on the project.
chief.ja: 最高の（chief financial officer：最高財務責任者）

chip.en: a small electronic part in computers
chip.ex: Every phone has a tiny computer chip inside.

code.ex: He wrote the code for the new game.

coding.ex: Many schools now teach coding to children.
coding.ja: コーディング；プログラミング

companies.ex: Many companies let staff work from home.

company.ex: My uncle works for a car company.

computer.ex: I use my computer for work every day.

consequently.ex: He missed the bus and consequently arrived late.

example.en: It snowed heavily; consequently, the school closed.
example.zh: 雪下得很大，因此學校停課了。

note.meaning: 因此；結果是。表示前面情況導致的結果。
note.usage: 正式連接副詞，常放在句首或分號後，後接逗號。

noteEn.meaning: as a result of what was just said.
noteEn.usage: A formal linking word, often at the start of a sentence or after a semicolon.

noteEs.exampleTr: Nevó mucho; por consiguiente, la escuela cerró.
noteEs.usage: Adverbio formal; suele ir al inicio de la oración o tras punto y coma.

noteHi.exampleTr: भारी बर्फ़ गिरी; परिणामस्वरूप, स्कूल बंद हो गया।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक शब्द; अक्सर वाक्य की शुरुआत में या अर्धविराम के बाद आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 大雪が降った。その結果、学校は休校になった。
noteJa.usage: 硬い接続副詞で、文頭やセミコロンの後に置くことが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 눈이 많이 내렸다. 그 결과 학교가 휴교했다.
noteKo.usage: 격식 있는 접속 부사로 문장 앞이나 세미콜론 뒤에 자주 쓴다.

considerable.ex: The repairs cost a considerable sum of money.

contended.en: said firmly that something is true
contended.ex: The lawyer contended that his client was innocent.

context.en: the situation in which something happens
context.ex: The decision makes sense in the context of the crisis.
context.zh: in the context of：在…的背景下

contingent.ex: The deal is contingent upon the bank's approval.

example.en: Your job offer is contingent upon a health check.
example.zh: 你的錄用要視健康檢查結果而定。

note.meaning: 取決於某條件；要看…而定。
note.usage: 常用 be contingent on/upon sth，多見於正式或商業、法律文件。

noteEn.meaning: depending on something else happening first.
noteEn.usage: Use 'be contingent on/upon something'; it is formal.

noteEs.exampleTr: Tu oferta de trabajo está supeditada a un examen médico.
noteEs.usage: Se usa be contingent on/upon sth, sobre todo en lenguaje formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: आपका नौकरी का प्रस्ताव स्वास्थ्य जाँच पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.usage: be contingent on/upon sth औपचारिक भाषा में आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: あなたの採用は健康診断の結果次第です。
noteJa.meaning: ある条件次第であること。
noteJa.usage: be contingent on/upon ～ の形で、主に硬い文章で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 당신의 채용 제안은 건강 검진 결과에 달려 있습니다.
noteKo.usage: be contingent on/upon ~ 형태로 격식 있는 글에서 주로 쓴다.

contrast.en: by contrast: showing a clear difference
contrast.ex: The city is noisy; the village, by contrast, is calm.

convened.en: brought people together for a meeting
convened.ex: The mayor convened an urgent meeting on flooding.
convened.ja: 招集された；開催された

example.en: The UN convened an emergency meeting on the crisis.
example.zh: 聯合國就這場危機召開了緊急會議。

note.usage: 主詞通常是政府、主席等主辦者；被動 be convened by 很常見。

noteEn.meaning: to bring people together for a formal meeting.
noteEn.usage: Used with 'meeting', 'summit', 'panel'; often passive: 'be convened by'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ONU convocó una reunión de emergencia sobre la crisis.
noteEs.meaning: convocar una reunión o un evento.
noteEs.usage: Suele tener como sujeto un gobierno o presidente; la pasiva be convened by es frecuente.

noteHi.exampleTr: संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने संकट पर एक आपात बैठक बुलाई।
noteHi.usage: आमतौर पर सरकार या अध्यक्ष बुलाते हैं; be convened by भी आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 国連はその危機について緊急会合を招集した。
noteJa.meaning: 会議などを招集・開催する。
noteJa.usage: 主語は政府や議長が多く、受動態 be convened by もよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 유엔은 그 위기에 관한 긴급 회의를 소집했다.
noteKo.usage: 주어는 주로 정부나 의장이며 수동태 be convened by도 흔하다.

council.en: a group that makes decisions or laws
council.ex: The council voted to build a new park.
council.zh: 理事會（Council of the EU：歐盟理事會）

creating.ex: The new factory is creating hundreds of jobs.
creating.hi: बना रहा है; पैदा कर रहा है

cybersecurity.ex: Banks spend a lot on cybersecurity.
cybersecurity.ja: サイバーセキュリティ

delegates.en: people sent to a meeting to represent others
delegates.ex: Delegates from forty countries attended the talks.

detecting.ex: This tool is good at detecting fake emails.

developers.ex: Developers are fixing the bugs in the app.

development.en: the work of creating new products
development.ex: The development of a new vaccine takes years.

discovery.en: finding something new, like a medicine
discovery.ex: The discovery of penicillin saved many lives.

do.ja: する（do better to：〜したほうがよい）
do.zh: would do better to：最好還是…

drug.ex: The new drug helps people with heart problems.

emphasise.ex: Teachers emphasise the need to read every day.

employment.ex: Employment in the town rose last year.

event.ex: The sports event attracted thousands of fans.

evolve.ex: Languages evolve as people use them.

example.en: something that shows what you mean
example.ex: Fruit, for example apples, is good for you.

excess.ex: The car reached speeds in excess of 200 km/h.

executive.en: a senior manager in a company

expansion.ex: The company plans an expansion into Asia.

extensive.ex: The museum has an extensive collection of paintings.

face.ex: Small shops face strong competition online.

fear.ex: Fear of failure stopped him from trying.

fertile.ex: Big cities are fertile ground for new businesses.
fertile.zh: fertile ground：沃土；大有可為之處

financial.ex: The firm is in financial trouble.

find.ex: Can you find the mistake in this sentence?

firms.ex: Local firms are hiring more staff.

fix.ex: Can you fix my bike this afternoon?

flaws.ex: The report found several flaws in the design.

focus.ex: Please focus on your homework now.

for.en: used to show purpose or who/what receives something

fresh.ex: The coach brought fresh ideas to the team.

from.en: showing where someone works or comes from

funding.ex: The project needs more funding to continue.

gathering.ex: It was a small family gathering.

generating.ex: Tourism is generating money for the village.

global.ex: Climate change is a global problem.

gone.ex: Bus fares have gone up again.

government.en: the group that runs a country
government.ex: The government will cut taxes next year.

governments.ex: Many governments signed the climate deal.

ground.ex: The internet is new ground for many older people.

grow.ex: Small businesses need help to grow.

growth.en: an increase in size or business
growth.ex: The country saw strong economic growth.

had.en: helping verb for the past perfect

has.en: helping verb for the present perfect
has.zh: （助動詞，現在完成式）已經；has yet to：尚未

held.ex: The wedding was held in a small church.

help.ex: Good sleep can help you study better.

highlighted.ex: The report highlighted the need for more teachers.

hinges.ex: The final result hinges on one vote.
hinges.ja: 〜次第である；〜にかかっている

example.en: Our trip hinges on the weather tomorrow.
example.zh: 我們的旅行取決於明天的天氣。

note.usage: 固定用 hinge on/upon sth，主詞多為結果、成敗或決定。

noteEs.exampleTr: Nuestro viaje depende del tiempo de mañana.
noteEs.usage: Siempre se usa hinge on/upon algo.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमारी यात्रा कल के मौसम पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी बात पर पूरी तरह निर्भर होना।
noteHi.usage: हमेशा hinge on/upon sth के रूप में आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 私たちの旅行は明日の天気次第だ。
noteJa.usage: 常に hinge on/upon ～ の形で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 우리 여행은 내일 날씨에 달려 있다.

hosted.ex: Paris hosted the Olympic Games in 2024.

household.ex: Keep household cleaning products away from children.

how.ex: She showed me how the machine works.

huge.ex: They won a huge prize in the lottery.

identifying.ex: Doctors are identifying the cause of the illness.

impact.ex: Phones have a big impact on sleep.

important.ex: Health is more important than money.

increased.ex: The number of tourists has increased this year.

industry.en: all the businesses making one kind of product
industry.ex: The car industry employs many people.

insisted.ex: He insisted that he had paid the bill.

intelligence.en: the ability to learn and think
intelligence.ex: Dolphins are known for their intelligence.

international.ex: She works for an international charity.

is.en: form of 'be' for he, she, it

jobs.ex: The new mall will bring many jobs.

lately.ex: I have been very busy lately.

leaders.ex: World leaders met to discuss climate change.

leads.ex: She leads a team of ten nurses.

legacy.ex: The bank still runs on legacy software.
legacy.zh: 舊有的（legacy code：舊版程式碼）

life.ex: She studies life on the ocean floor.

looks.en: looks after: takes care of; is in charge of
looks.ex: My sister looks after the family's money.

machine.ex: This machine makes coffee in one minute.
machine.zh: 機器（at machine speed：以機器的速度）

made.ex: The shop made a small profit last month.

maintained.en: said strongly that something is true
maintained.ex: He maintained that he was at home all evening.

maintaining.en: keeping something at the same level

make.ex: Loud noises make my dog nervous.
make.zh: 使（人害怕）；make a profit：獲利

manufacturing.ex: Car manufacturing is important to the region.

medicine.ex: She wants to study medicine at university.

meeting.en: an event where people talk together
meeting.ex: We have a meeting every Monday morning.

microchip.ex: Each pet has a microchip with its details.

milk.ex: I put milk in my tea.

model.ex: Their business model depends on free apps.

move.en: an action to start something new
move.ex: The move into online sales helped the shop.

ms.en: a title used before a woman's name

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

new.ex: She bought a new phone yesterday.

not.ex: I am not ready to leave yet.

notably.ex: Notably, prices fell for the first time in years.

note.en: a tone or feeling in what someone says
note.ex: The speech ended on a hopeful note.
note.zh: struck a … note：採取…的語調／態度

noted.ex: The teacher noted that attendance had improved.

number.ex: The number of cars in the city keeps rising.

observed.ex: She observed that the room was very cold.

observing.ex: He smiled, observing that the plan had worked.

occupations.ex: Nursing is one of the most trusted occupations.

officer.en: a person with an important job
officer.ex: The officer in charge signed the papers.

old.ex: He still uses an old laptop.

older.ex: Older phones may not get updates.

openai.en: the US company that makes ChatGPT

opportunities.ex: The city offers many opportunities for artists.

organised.ex: The students organised a charity concert.

out.ex: She pointed out a mistake in my essay.
out.ja: 指摘する（point out）；選び出す（single out）

part.ex: The trip is part of our school project.
part.zh: as part of：作為…的一部分

patching.ex: The team is patching the bug tonight.
patching.ja: パッチを当てること；修正

peddle.en: try to sell or push an idea
peddle.ex: Some websites peddle false health advice.

people.ex: Many people walk to work here.

pharmaceutical.ex: She works for a pharmaceutical company.

place.ex: The race will take place on Sunday.

pointing.en: pointing out: saying a fact to show something
pointing.ex: He left early, pointing out that he was tired.

post.ex: The bank will post its results next week.
post.zh: post a profit：公布獲利；實現盈利

potential.en: ability to develop in the future
potential.ex: This young player has great potential.

practical.ex: We need practical ideas to save energy.

presidency.en: the time when a country leads a group
presidency.ex: Spain held the presidency for six months.

president.ex: The president of the club gave a speech.

pressed.ex: Pressed for an answer, he finally agreed.

problems.ex: We solved all the problems together.

profit.ex: The café made a profit in its first year.

profitable.ex: The small bakery quickly became profitable.

programming.ex: He took an online course in programming.

promising.ex: Early test results look very promising.

public.ex: Public interest in the story grew quickly.

raised.ex: The school raised money for new books.

raising.ex: They are raising funds for the hospital.

ranks.en: all the people in a group
ranks.ex: The ranks of electric car owners are growing.

rapidly.ex: The fire spread rapidly through the forest.

rather.ex: I would rather walk than take the bus.

rds.en: a large event venue in Dublin
rds.zh: RDS（都柏林皇家都柏林學會展館）

recent.ex: Recent changes made the app easier to use.

rectifying.ex: The company is rectifying the error on your bill.
rectifying.ja: 是正すること；修正すること

example.en: The airline promised to rectify the booking error.
example.zh: 航空公司承諾會修正訂位錯誤。

note.usage: 正式用語，受詞常為 mistake、error、problem、situation。

noteEn.meaning: to correct something that is wrong.

noteEs.exampleTr: La aerolínea prometió corregir el error de la reserva.
noteEs.usage: Verbo formal; suele llevar mistake, error, problem.

noteHi.exampleTr: एयरलाइन ने बुकिंग की ग़लती सुधारने का वादा किया।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक शब्द; mistake, error, problem के साथ आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 航空会社は予約の誤りを訂正すると約束した。
noteJa.usage: 硬い語で、目的語は mistake、error、problem などが多い。

noteKo.usage: 격식 있는 동사로 mistake, error, problem 등을 목적어로 쓴다.

regard.ex: With regard to your question, I will reply tomorrow.

regulated.ex: Banks are strictly regulated by the state.

reinforce.ex: Practice will reinforce what you learned in class.

remarking.ex: She laughed, remarking that the cake looked strange.

repairing.ex: He spent the day repairing the roof.

rigorous.ex: New drugs go through rigorous testing.

example.en: All new cars must pass rigorous safety tests.
example.zh: 所有新車都必須通過嚴格的安全測試。

note.usage: 常修飾 testing、standards、regulation 等名詞，語氣比 strict 更正式。

noteEn.usage: Often used with 'testing', 'standards' or 'regulation'; more formal than 'strict'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Todos los coches nuevos deben superar rigurosas pruebas de seguridad.
noteEs.usage: Acompaña a testing, standards, regulation; más formal que strict.

noteHi.exampleTr: सभी नई कारों को कठोर सुरक्षा परीक्षण पास करने होंगे।
noteHi.meaning: बहुत सख़्त और पूरी तरह से।
noteHi.usage: testing, standards, regulation जैसे शब्दों के साथ आता है; strict से ज़्यादा औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新車はすべて厳格な安全試験に合格しなければならない。
noteJa.usage: testing、standards、regulation などを修飾し、strict より硬い語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 모든 신차는 엄격한 안전 테스트를 통과해야 한다.
noteKo.usage: testing, standards, regulation 등과 함께 쓰이며 strict보다 격식 있다.

roles.ex: The company is hiring for several new roles.

route.ex: University is not the only route into a good job.

rules.en: official instructions about what is allowed
rules.ex: Players must follow the rules of the game.

safeguards.en: rules or actions that protect people
safeguards.ex: The law includes safeguards for children online.

example.en: The new law adds safeguards against data theft.
example.zh: 新法律增加了防止資料竊取的保障措施。

note.usage: 常與 against 連用（safeguards against sth），也可作動詞 safeguard「保護」。

noteEn.meaning: rules or actions that protect people from harm.
noteEn.usage: Often 'safeguards against something'; 'safeguard' is also a verb.

noteEs.exampleTr: La nueva ley añade salvaguardias contra el robo de datos.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir con against: safeguards against algo; el verbo safeguard es «proteger».

noteHi.exampleTr: नया क़ानून डेटा चोरी के ख़िलाफ़ सुरक्षा उपाय जोड़ता है।
noteHi.meaning: सुरक्षा के लिए बनाए गए नियम या उपाय।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर against के साथ: safeguards against sth; क्रिया safeguard = रक्षा करना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい法律はデータ盗難に対する保護措置を追加している。
noteJa.meaning: 保護のための措置や規定。
noteJa.usage: safeguards against ～ の形が多い。動詞 safeguard は「守る」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 법은 데이터 도난에 대한 보호 조치를 추가한다.
noteKo.usage: safeguards against ~ 형태가 흔하며 동사 safeguard는 '보호하다'.

paragraphs: A big meeting about artificial intelligence (AI) took place in Dublin on Wednesday. Leaders from companies and governments came. Ireland organised it because it leads the EU Council this year.

Sarah Friar works for OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. She looks after its money. She said AI companies should not try to make people afraid. They should show how AI can solve problems, for example in computer safety.
More than 2.5 million people in Ireland use ChatGPT every week. OpenAI is very big, but it does not make a profit yet.
Brad Smith from Microsoft also spoke. He said there are more safety rules for ovens than for AI. He wants stronger rules. He said people are more important than AI.

AI companies should sell solutions and not fear, a top OpenAI executive told an international AI summit in Dublin on Wednesday. The government organised the event at the RDS as part of Ireland's presidency of the Council of the European Union.

Sarah Friar, OpenAI's chief financial officer, said AI could help in areas like cybersecurity. For example, it can find weak points in old computer code and fix them very quickly. She also sees chances to grow in medicine, drug development and the computer chip industry.
Asked about jobs, she said the number of software developers around the world has gone up. The way people learn these skills may change, but AI is also creating new jobs.
More than 2.5 million people in Ireland use ChatGPT every week. OpenAI has raised huge amounts of money, but it has not made a profit yet. This year it started selling adverts on ChatGPT.
Microsoft president Brad Smith also spoke. He said there are more safety rules for ovens and milk cartons than for AI, and he called for stronger rules.

Artificial intelligence companies should focus on selling solutions rather than fear, OpenAI's chief financial officer told an international AI summit in Dublin on Wednesday. The event, held at the RDS, was organised by the Government as part of Ireland's presidency of the Council of the EU.

Sarah Friar said AI could strengthen cybersecurity by detecting weaknesses in older code and repairing them at machine speed. She added that the company saw opportunities for growth in life sciences, drug development and the microchip industry.
On employment, she said the number of software developers worldwide had increased, and that while the way people learn to code might change, AI was also generating new roles.

More than 2.5 million people in Ireland use ChatGPT each week. OpenAI has raised over $180 billion but has yet to turn a profit, and this year it began selling advertising on the chatbot. Ms Friar said trust was central to that model.
Microsoft president Brad Smith used his speech to call for tougher AI safety rules, pointing out that ovens and milk cartons face more regulation than AI.

AI firms would do better to peddle solutions than to stoke fear, OpenAI's chief financial officer told delegates at an international AI summit in Dublin on Wednesday. The gathering at the RDS was hosted by the Government under the banner of Ireland's EU Council presidency.

Sarah Friar contended that AI could shore up cybersecurity by unearthing flaws in legacy code and patching them at machine speed. She also singled out life sciences, drug discovery and semiconductors as fertile ground for expansion.

Pressed on the technology's impact on employment, she noted that the global ranks of software developers had swelled, and argued that, although the route into coding might shift, AI was spawning fresh roles.

Some 2.5 million people in Ireland turn to ChatGPT weekly. Yet despite amassing more than $180 billion in funding, OpenAI has still to post a profit, and it has lately ventured into advertising, a model Ms Friar insisted hinges on trust.
Microsoft president Brad Smith struck a more cautious note, urging stricter safeguards and remarking that ovens and milk cartons are more tightly regulated than AI.
